title: Compatible etale scheme charts recognize unramified and etale morphisms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to Y$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. In a compatible chart diagram $b h=f a$, the objects $U,V$ are schemes, $a:U\to X$ and $b:V\to Y$ are representable etale morphisms, and $h:U\to V$ is a scheme morphism. Scheme unramifiedness and etaleness mean [def-weil-unramified-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. The corresponding chartwise property of $f$ means that $h$ has that scheme property for every compatible chart diagram. For either property, it suffices to test a single compatible diagram with $a$ surjective: $f$ has the chartwise property if and only if its $h$ has the scheme property. For every prescribed surjective etale scheme atlas $b:V\to Y$, there exist a scheme $U$, a surjective etale scheme atlas $a:U\to X$, and $h:U\to V$ with $b h=f a$. These assertions include empty spaces and schemes and require no separation or finiteness hypotheses on $f$.

proof.text: For unramifiedness, use the three clauses of [lem-sfb-scheme-unramified-etale-locality], interchanging the final two existential binders to obtain IsEtaleLocalOnSourceAndTarget. For etaleness take the first conjunct of [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties]. The unramified property respects isomorphisms because it is the intersection of locally finite type with the diagonal of open immersions; etaleness respects isomorphisms by Mathlib. Apply [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion]. A given diagram with surjective source and P(h) witnesses HasEtalePresentationProperty; in the other direction apply MapIsLocally directly to the given diagram. Target-chart surjectivity is not used.

proof.text: Choose an atlas c:h_W -> X from [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Apply the scheme-test definition of IsEtale b to c followed by f. It produces U, p:U -> W and q:h_U -> h_V with a representing pullback square, and p is etale. The IsSurjective b test may choose a different representing scheme, but the unique isomorphism of the two pullback squares, reflected through fully faithful Yoneda [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful], transports surjectivity to p. Let h be the Yoneda preimage of q and a=yoneda(p) followed by c. For either scheme property P=etale or surjective, yoneda(p) is representable with P: represent a test by the scheme pullback [def-pc-fibre-product], use preservation of pullbacks by Yoneda, and use scheme base change [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. Composite representable etaleness is isEtale_comp from [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For composite representable surjectivity, successively represent the two scheme tests and paste the squares; their scheme projection is surjective by [lem-trf-surjective-morphism-composition]. Etaleness of the analogous composite projection is [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. The original representing square gives the required commuting equation. No algebraic-space fibre-product or point-set covering theorem is needed.

proof.text: All arguments are uniform for empty schemes and spaces: existence of the starting atlas and every representing test is part of the hypotheses or [def-trf-algebraic-space], and no point is selected. Scheme locality includes empty sources by [lem-sfb-scheme-unramified-etale-locality, lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties]. Thus no extra hypothesis on nonemptiness, separation, finiteness, quasi-compactness or Noetherianity occurs.
